eli5.text: The part of the system that writes out code patches for users was switched to a newer, specially tuned version of the AI model. This only affects the behind-the-scenes generation of those patches and doesn't change anything you can see directly. If you happened to look at how the patch-generation step is wired up, you'd see the old model reference is now commented out and replaced by the new one.

ai.title: Improve patch context matching in applyPatch
ai.summary: Refactored `applyPatch` in `common/src/util/patch.ts` to use a multi-stage context matching strategy involving hunk headers and trimmed whitespace comparison. Replaced inline parsing with extracted helper logic to handle cases where strict line numbers fail, falling back to headline indices or trimmed matches. This increases resilience against minor file drift or formatting differences during patch application. Added `test:patch` script to `package.json` for targeted verification.

eli5.text: When you apply an edit to a file, the editor now uses several smarter strategies to find the right spot in the file, instead of relying only on the exact line number. This means edits are more likely to apply successfully even if the file has shifted a little or has different spacing. You would notice fewer edits failing when files have minor changes or formatting differences. This is live today.

ai.title: Patch apply guards against out-of-bounds line index
ai.summary: applyPatch in common/src/util/patch.ts adds bounds checks before comparing oldIndex against lines.length. Prevents crash when a '-' line references a position past the file end. Fuzzy match loop also breaks early if oldIndex + j exceeds array length. Covers core patch utility used by all surfaces.

eli5.text: The system that applies suggested edits to your files no longer crashes when an edit tries to remove a line that doesn't exist near the end of a file. If you use the "assistant deletes a comment" or "assistant rewrites code" features, edits that previously errored out with a position past the last line now safely skip that invalid removal instead of failing. No new behavior was added for typical edits, but mismatched or out-of-range deletions are handled gracefully rather than breaking the update.

ai.title: Append assistant edits to response and truncate large user diffs
ai.summary: Backend appends assistant-made changes to the response message within `<edits_made_by_assistant>` tags. CLI truncates user edit diffs exceeding 40k chars to `[LARGE_FILE_CHANGE_TOO_LONG_TO_REPRODUCE]` before formatting. Updates `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` and `npm-app/src/cli.ts`.

eli5.text: When the assistant makes edits to your files, those changes are now included at the end of its response in a dedicated section, so you can see what it modified in one place. If a file you changed in a previous session is very large (over 40,000 characters), the system will shorten your past edits in the conversation history to just a placeholder note saying the change was too big to show, rather than pasting the entire file. This affects anyone reviewing or continuing a coding session where large files were edited. This is live today.
